newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOWE WINS AGAIN ON GOLOTA'S DISQUALIFICATION.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOWE WINS AGAIN ON GOLOTA'S DISQUALIFICATION.

text.p: For the second time in five months Riddick Bowe, behind on all three judges' scorecards, benefitted from Andrew Golota's uncontrollable penchant for throwing low blows and won on disqualification on Saturday.

Golota had a point deducted for an intentional head butt in the second round, lost another point for a low blow in the fourth round and was disqualified at 2:58 of the ninth round after sending Bowe to the canvas with another low blow.

"He was warned, and I took away a point for a head butt earlier and I took another point away for a low blow that was really blatant and then the third low blow, and that's a disqualification," said referee Eddie Cotton.
Golota, 28, was taken to the hospital immediately after the fight with a suspected broken jaw, said his spokesman, Mike Boorman.
Bowe, 29, improved to 40-1, while Golota slipped to 28-2.
The fight was a crowd-pleasing slugfest as the two heavyweights, often looking exhausted, slugged it out with wild punches.
Bowe was knocked down twice and Golota once.

Golota, who also was disqualified in the seventh round on July 11 after repeated low blows, knocked down Bowe with a right and a left to the head that dropped the former heavyweight champion to the canvas in the second round.
Bowe got up and Golota continued pummeling him around the ring. But Golota had a cut open underneath his left eyebrow.

Bowe, who lost at least 45 pounds (20 kg) since last September to weigh in at an almost emaciated-looking 235 pounds (106.6 kg) Thursday, came on in the fourth round, catching Golota with a flurry of combinations that knocked the Pole down for the first time in his career.
Golota got to his feet quickly and almost immediately started throwing very low blows, for which he was warned.
Finally Bowe went down after one of the low blows and the referee took a point away and Bowe took about a minute to recover. He could have taken up to five minutes.
"I don't want you to go to the body anymore. Everything goes to the head," Golota's co-trainer, Lou Duva, said between the fourth and fifth rounds.

In the fifth round, Bowe seemed exhausted and was throwing lazy, looping punches. Golota caught Bowe with a rash of punches up against the ropes. Bowe came off the ropes and Golota sent him reeling with another combination, ending with a right to the head.
It seemed to be all Golota after that, with Bowe at times seeming so tired he was having difficulty standing up.
Bowe seemed only a faded image of his old self Saturday. But it really didn't matter as Golota beat himself again.
In a bout to determine the shouting rights as the man champions most want to avoid, Ray Mercer won a 10-round unanimous decision over former heavyweight champion Tim Witherspoon.
The steel-jawed Mercer, who narrowly lost a 10-round decision to Lennox Lewis last May and last won a fight in 1993, beat Witherspoon in the late rounds by landing the strongest punches.
Mercer improved to 24-4-1. Witherspoon fell to 45-5.
